title: The Lie algebra of a normal closed subgroup is an ideal
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field]. Let $G,N$ be affine $k$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $i:N\hookrightarrow G$ be a closed normal subgroup inclusion [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Write $\mathfrak g=T_{G/k,e_G}$ and $\mathfrak n=T_{N/k,e_N}$ for their identity tangent spaces [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space, def-sc-dual-numbers], equipped with the canonical Lie brackets induced by group commutators [def-wf-lie-algebra]. The differential $di:\mathfrak n\to\mathfrak g$ is an injective homomorphism of finite-dimensional $k$-Lie algebras. Its image $I=di(\mathfrak n)$ is an ideal of $\mathfrak g$, that is, $[\mathfrak g,I]\subseteq I$. If $N$ is commutative as a group scheme, then $\mathfrak n$ has zero bracket, and hence $[I,I]=0$. No smoothness, reducedness, connectedness, perfectness or characteristic restriction is imposed.

source.place: 10.12 (p.190), 10.14 (p.190), 10.19--10.22 and Theorem 10.23 (pp.192--193): tangent injection, conjugation action on Lie(N), and its differential. Lemma 23.68 (p.506) explicitly uses the commutative-normal-subgroup specialization. No Stacks tag states the normal-subgroup Lie-ideal assertion.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus], $\mathfrak n$ and $\mathfrak g$ are finite dimensional and $di$ is a $k$-linear Lie homomorphism. By [lem-sfb-affine-group-dual-number-calculus], $di$ is injective. We use that node's notation $E_{J,R}(v)$ for the dual-number point of $J$ attached to $v\in\operatorname{Lie}(J)\otimes_k R$; its naturality identifies $i(E_{N,R}(v))$ with $E_{G,R}((di\otimes1)v)$.

Choose a faithful closed embedding $\rho:G\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}$ by [lem-sfb-affine-group-faithful-linear-representation]. Its differential is injective by [lem-sfb-affine-group-dual-number-calculus]. Fix $x\in\mathfrak g$, $y\in\mathfrak n$ and put $z=di(y)$, $X=d\rho(x)$, $Y=d\rho(z)$. By [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus], $d\rho([x,z])=XY-YX$. Set $A=k[\epsilon,\delta]/(\epsilon^2,\delta^2)$ and $D=k[\eta]/(\eta^2)$. Base change $E_{G,k}(x)$ along $\eta\mapsto\epsilon$ and $E_{N,k}(y)$ along $\eta\mapsto\delta$, and denote the resulting points by $a\in G(A)$, $b\in N(A)$. Naturality gives $\rho(a)=1+\epsilon X$ and $\rho(i(b))=1+\delta Y$. Multiplying these matrices and their inverses $1-\epsilon X$, $1-\delta Y$ gives
$$\rho(ai(b)a^{-1}i(b)^{-1})=(1+\epsilon X+\delta Y+\epsilon\delta XY)(1-\epsilon X)(1-\delta Y)=1+\epsilon\delta(XY-YX).$$
The same is the image under $\rho$ of $q=E_{G,k}([x,z])\in G(D)$ after $j:D\to A$, $\eta\mapsto\epsilon\delta$. Injectivity of $\rho_A$ therefore identifies $G(j)(q)$ with this commutator.

source.place: 10.11, 10.19 and proof of Theorem 10.23, printed pp.189,192--193; explicit two-parameter commutator expansion

proof.text: Normality in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], applied to the algebra $A$, implies $ai(b)a^{-1}i(b)^{-1}\in i(N(A))$. We descend this membership to $q\in G(D)$ explicitly. Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion], $i$ is given by a surjection $C\to C/J$ with $N=\operatorname{Spec}(C/J)$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $q$ is a $k$-algebra map $\phi:C\to D$, and its base change belongs to $N(A)$ precisely when $j\phi(J)=0$. The map $j$ is injective: $1,\epsilon,\delta,\epsilon\delta$ are a $k$-basis of $A$, so $c+d\eta\mapsto c+d\epsilon\delta$ has zero kernel. Thus $\phi(J)=0$ and $\phi$ factors uniquely through $C/J$. The resulting point of $N(D)$ reduces to its identity, since its image in $G(k)$ is the identity and $i_k$ is injective. By [lem-sfb-affine-group-dual-number-calculus], this point is $E_{N,k}(w)$ for some $w\in\mathfrak n$, and naturality and injectivity of $E_{G,k}$ give $di(w)=[x,di(y)]$. Consequently the linear subspace $I=di(\mathfrak n)$ satisfies $[\mathfrak g,I]\subseteq I$, the ideal condition of [def-wf-lie-algebra].

source.place: Lemma 23.68, printed p.506, normal-ideal assertion; explicit closed-subgroup descent using Stacks Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion), literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex

proof.text: Suppose $N$ is commutative. For $u,v\in\mathfrak n$ put $U=d\rho(di(u))$, $V=d\rho(di(v))$. The two tangent points of $N$ over $A$ commute, so their images under $\rho i$ have commutator $1$. The multiplication in step 2 gives $1+\epsilon\delta(UV-VU)=1$; independence of the basis coefficient $\epsilon\delta$ gives $UV-VU=0$. Bracket preservation in [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus] now gives $d\rho(di([u,v]))=0$. Both differentials are injective by [lem-sfb-affine-group-dual-number-calculus], hence $[u,v]=0$. Finally $[di(u),di(v)]=di([u,v])=0$, proving $[I,I]=0$.
